source: A research philosophy refers to the set of beliefs and assumptions concerning the nature of knowledge and how that knowledge can be developed through research (Saunders, Lewis, & Thornhill, 2019). This study was underpinned by the positivist research philosophy. Positivism holds that reality exists independently of the researcher and can be studied objectively through observation and measurement, and that knowledge is considered valid only when it is derived from empirical evidence that can be tested and verified (Bryman, 2016). The positivist paradigm was considered appropriate for this study because the research sought to measure two quantifiable constructs, namely TikTok use and self-esteem, and to establish the statistical relationship between them. Positivism further emphasises objectivity, structured instrumentation, and the use of statistical procedures to test relationships between variables, all of which were central to the aims of this study. Adopting a positivist stance allowed the researcher to remain detached from the phenomenon under investigation and to rely on standardised instruments and numerical data rather than subjective interpretation, thereby enhancing the objectivity and replicability of the findings.

By taking a positivist stance, the researcher was able to remain detached from the phenomenon under investigation and to rely on standardised instruments and numerical data rather than subjective interpretation. This approach strengthened the objectivity and replicability of the findings.
